faults.detail: "Palindrom" is misspelt (should be "Palindrome"). It is a label string in the spec, although this round does not show it.

notes: The mix-up is zero not being even. The round draws 10 numbers from 0-30 (lo 0, hi 30, seed 271, hitRate 0.5), but the packet does not show whether 0 (or 10/20) is actually among them, so I cannot tell whether a child with that belief meets the case where it goes wrong. The round title and sub-title are generic and do not point at zero. The counter shows "Kat gaya 0/4" while count is 10 with hitRate 0.5; how the engine reaches 4 targets cannot be checked from the packet.

Wave 1 uses ticks 8 for 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 and wave 2 uses ticks 6 for 1/6, 1/3, so every item lands on a tick. Placing 1/8 nearest 0, with 1/4 and 1/2 further along, shows where the 'bigger bottom number = bigger fraction' belief goes wrong. The subs ('Har item ko pakdo', 'Ek ek item pakdo') only say what to do. In both screenshots the catcher starts near the first 1/8 tick but not on it (pointer at about x=208 against the tick at about x=197 at p412). From one still frame I cannot tell whether this is the engine's default start position or a hint, so I have not counted it.

Round is rule 'multiple', a=6, lo 1..hi 48, count 18, hitRate 0.5; the screen shows 'CHUNA GAYA 0/9' (9 targets) while 1-48 holds only 8 distinct multiples of 6 (6..48), so the engine must repeat a value; from the packet alone I cannot tell whether that is intended or whether distractors include the factors of 6 (1, 2, 3) that would surface the factor/multiple mix-up. Neither counted as a fault.

The engine's grading of how close a cut must be ("Kaafi paas" against "Bilkul sahi") is not in the packet, so I could not check from the packet whether a cut into clearly unequal parts gets enough feedback to correct the unequal-parts mix-up. Every wave has marks false, and each title and sub-title agrees with its items (3, 4, and a mix of 3 and 4 parts). The pieces are strips (patti), not round things. No rule or answer is stated.

Screen counter reads 'HO GAYA 0/1' beside 'DAURA 1/2'; the packet does not say what the '1' counts (per-round task or whole run), so not counted. Rounds 1/2+1/3 and 1/4+1/4 directly test the add-across mix-up (2/5, 2/8); no title or sub names the method or the answer.

Round 1 '20 se 5 kam' rule -5: 20,30,50,80 -> 15,25,45,75 correct, with -20 tile as the word-order trap. Round 2 'Har din 3 rupaye kam' rule -3 is correct but has no 'X se Y kam' phrase, so it only weakly probes the word-order mix-up; round 1 carries it. The conveyor bar passes behind '80' and '75' but they stay legible.
